card.title: Relation Between Angle of Prism, Minimum Deviation and Refractive Index

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Prism optics rest on two relations. First, the **deviation relation**: δ = (i − r₁) + (e − r₂) with the geometry identity $r_1 + r_2 = A$ gives $\delta = i + e - A$ (NEB 2024, 4m). Second, at minimum deviation the symmetric passage (i = e, r₁ = r₂ = A/2) plus Snell's law yields the **prism formula** $n = \frac{\sin\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}$ (NEB 2024, 5m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - δ = i + e − A; r₁ + r₂ = A - δm = 2i − A at minimum - n = sin((A+δm)/2)/sin(A/2)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Minimum Deviation Condition: i = e, r₁ = r₂ = A/2, ray inside parallel to base — only at this symmetric position is D = D_min.  ·  Small Angle Approximation: D ≈ (μ-1)A valid only for small A (typically < 10°) and small angles of incidence.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The refractive index of the prism material is given by the sine ratio of half the sum (A + δm) to half the prism angle."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **r₁ + r₂ = A** — the prism-angle identity that converts two-face geometry into one equation.  ·  **At δm:** δm = 2i − A, so i = (A + δm)/2 — half-angles everywhere in the prism formula.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Prism Formula Combine prism geometry with minimum-deviation symmetry and a powerful result drops out: $n = \frac{\sin\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}$. It is how spectrometers measure refractive index, and NEB 2024 carried it as a 5-mark derivation plus a numerical.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Deviation relation δ = i + e − A (NEB 2024, 4m) At the first face the ray deviates by (i − r₁); at the second by (e − r₂). Total deviation: $$\delta = (i - r_1) + (e - r_2) = (i + e) - (r_1 + r_2)$$ From the quadrilateral geometry inside the prism (the two normals meet at the prism angle A): $$r_1 + r_2 = A \Rightarrow \boxed{\delta = i + e - A}$$ ### 2.2 The prism…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (4m): A prism of A = 60° and n = 1.6 is set at minimum deviation. Find δm.** — sin((60+δm)/2) = 1.6 sin 30° = 0.8 → (60+δm)/2 = 53.13° → δm = 46.3°.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The 2024 5m derivation expects: symmetry conditions → δm = 2i − A → Snell → formula.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The prism formula is Snell's law dressed in minimum-deviation symmetry** — the spectrometer's measuring principle.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: δ = i + e − A; n = sin((A+δm)/2)/sin(A/2).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Precision spectrometers measure n to 5 decimal places using this formula — the foundation of historical glassmaking tables.
